title: Bessie Smith's show and the night before her death
summary: He joined Broadway Rastus, Winstead's show, with Bessie Smith; they played Darling, Mississippi, and she and her husband left ahead in a car.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, that's what I want to ask you in detail, if you don't mind telling that, because there'd been several rumors, you know, published. Well, some of the people...
It was 1937 that she was killed. 1937. Now, let's see, it was in 37. We were, we had about three more weeks off before we were going in.
If you don't mind, start at the beginning, when did you get into this show, and was she, was Bessie the star of it when you joined it, or how was it?
Well, Bessie met us on the, she came to the show, I was already on the show.
Yeah.
When she came to the show, she came to the show... It was called the Broadway... Broadway Rastus.
Broadway Rastus.
It was a show that belonged to Old Man Winstead, E.S. Winstead, out of Fayetteville, North Carolina.
Yeah.
So he had two shows on the road, see, and he had a guy managing this show that Bessie was on, see.
Yeah.

Bessie used to do concerts on the show, see. I and her husband were there together, you know. And we had about, oh, I imagine around about two more weeks out, I would say, before closing, see, because it was getting cold, you know, we were in there playing the Delta, the little towns in the Delta, Mississippi. And it was, you played in those smaller towns on a Saturday night because on a Saturday all the people mostly would come to town to get their groceries
and things, you know, a big crowd with wagons and horses and everybody wanted to see

the show that night. And this was in Darling, Mississippi that we played that night. And after the show it rained. So I used to drive the bus, you know, extra, with 35 people on the bus and the fellas, I mean, some of the fellas used to drive, like drive a truck or something, make extra money to keep them high and extra help, you see. And, well, Bessie and them used to leave ahead of us, you see.
They'd leave in the car. They'd leave in the car.
No, they had a nice, they had a packet.
Yeah, but I mean, it wasn't, they didn't drive on the bus, I mean, no, they rode in the car,

see. Her husband drove, I mean, she rode along with him, see. And they had a pink packet, nice little car. And they were about, I imagine, about an hour ahead of us, an hour, hour and a half ahead of us. When we were leaving there, we were going to, to Highlands, Highlandsdale, Mississippi, you see.
Yeah.
And we had showed this town, uh, uh, Clarksdale before, see, so we were supposed to pass through Clarksdale.
Yeah.
Well, this accident happened around about ten miles out of Clarksdale before you get to Clarksdale,
you see.
